learning_objective: 🌿 Appreciate the profound, unwritten oral literature of India's indigenous tribes, which celebrates life, nature, and community ownership!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: मौखिक परंपरा (जो लिखा न गया हो, केवल बोला जाता हो)
हाशिए पर (समाज के मुख्य वर्ग से कटे हुए लोग)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Unlike mainstream literature, tribal literature is strictly oral. It is not printed in books but lives in the memory, songs, and daily conversations of the tribal people. It is passed down through generations by word of mouth.

Tribal verses do not view nature as something to be conquered. Instead, they treat trees, rivers, mountains, and animals as equal companions. Their songs express deep reverence and harmony with the natural world.

In tribal literature, there is no 'author'. You won't find a signature at the end of a song. The songs belong to the entire community. Art is not a private property or a profession; it is a shared way of life.

Tribal life is enveloped in verse. They have specific songs for birth, death, marriage, sowing seeds, harvesting, and even for everyday chores. Their poetry is incredibly functional and tied to survival and joy.
G.N. Devy highlights a tragedy: as modern development encroaches on forests and mainstream languages dominate, these ancient tribal languages and their beautiful verses are rapidly dying out.

fun_activity.title: 🗣️ The Telephone Game
fun_activity.instructions: Oral literature relies purely on memory! Sit with 5 friends. Whisper a long, poetic sentence into the first person's ear. Let them whisper it to the next. See how much the sentence changes by the time it reaches the last person. That's the fluid nature of oral verse!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly contrast mainstream literature (written, individual authorship, commercial) with tribal literature (oral, collective ownership, deeply integrated into daily life).
📌 Use the term 'Ecocentric' (nature-centered) to describe the tribal worldview in your answers.
📌 Mention that saving tribal verse is not just about saving poems; it's about saving an entire worldview and thousands of years of ecological knowledge.
quick_recap: ⭐ Tribal communities do not separate art from life; singing and dancing are natural parts of working and living.
⭐ There is no 'copyright' in tribal verse; the songs evolve continuously as different people sing them.
⭐ G.N. Devy is a prominent linguist who has worked extensively to document and save dying Indian languages.
